model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between Co-occurrence Number and ACC (%), showing how different methods compare in terms of accuracy as co-occurrence increases. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number, with a logarithmic scale ranging from 3 to 3,000, marked at intervals of 10, 100, and 1,000. The y-axis represents ACC (%), with a linear scale from 40 to 65, marked at intervals of 5. The plot displays six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black, circle, solid), FT (blue, down-triangle, solid), IKE (red, up-triangle, solid), MEND (brown, diamond, solid), MEMIT (purple, diamond, solid), and ROME (green, square, solid). The Base line starts at around 39% at a co-occurrence number of 3 and increases to approximately 45% at 3,000. The FT line begins at around 41% and rises to about 49%. The IKE line starts at roughly 43% and reaches 50%. The MEND line begins at approximately 45% and increases to around 56%. The MEMIT line starts at about 46% and goes up to 55%. The ROME line begins at roughly 51% and rises to 65%. All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend as the Co-occurrence Number grows.
